paper-2.purpose: Inset panels, code ground, demos, hero plate.

ink-2.purpose: Secondary text, captions, default borders, layer tags.

rule.purpose: 1px rules, leader lines, plate borders at rest.

signal.purpose: The one thing to look at now: primary CTA, focus ring, active rail step, selected part, edge traces.

human.purpose: Only where a person approves, denies, accepts or authorizes.

label.purpose: Part numbers, commands, code, status chip. Not running prose.

shadows.name: sheet-lift
shadows.purpose: Mobile inspector bottom sheet below 768px. The only shadow in the build.

motion.name: reduced-motion-collapse
motion.purpose: Under prefers-reduced-motion. No other CSS transitions exist; the exploded view is a pure function of scroll.

darkMode.note: Values are in colorMeta.darkValue. Dark is derived from the same system ('drawing on slate').

narrative.overview: The page is a precise, annotated technical illustration printed on warm drafting paper. Its one dense moment is the exploded view: a real Workbench capture separates into layers, and capability cartridges stand on an oblique shelf with part numbers, leader lines and an inspector column. Everything around that moment is quiet: a single text column at 68ch, hairline rules between beats, generous vertical rhythm, and real captures shown bare with a caption. The system is light-first; dark ('drawing on slate') is the same system inverted. It rejects purple or blue AI gradients, glowing brains, neural node clouds, particle fields, fake browser, terminal or IDE chrome, icon-over-heading three-card grids, hero metric tiles, and dark-first neon.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper ground with a cool graphite ink; contrast carries hierarchy, not color.
One signal accent (drafting orange) marks the single thing to look at now.
One human accent (decision green-teal) appears only where a person decides.
Hairline rules (1px) and flat surfaces; depth is tonal, not shadowed.
Newsreader for voice, Hanken Grotesk for text, Martian Mono for part numbers and commands.
Cartridges and leader lines are the only illustrative vocabulary; no other iconography.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Drafting Orange marks the one thing the reader should look at now. Its rarity is the point.

rules.name: The Person Decides Rule
rules.body: Decision Green-Teal appears only where a human approves, denies, accepts or authorizes an extension.

rules.name: The Measure Rule
rules.body: Running text stops at 68ch. Wide things (captures, the stage, code) may be wide; prose is not.

rules.name: The Mono Is For Identifiers Rule
rules.body: Martian Mono sets part numbers, commands, code and status. It does not set running sentences.

rules.name: The Flat Paper Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. Depth is a tonal step or a hairline, never a drop shadow. A shadow is allowed only where a surface overlays content it describes.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Structure is drawn with 1px lines in Hairline Stone. Selected or active items take a 2px Drafting Orange or Graphite stroke, not a glow.

dos: Do set running text at 18px / 1.6 on desktop, 17px below 768px, with a 68ch measure.
Do use Drafting Orange for at most one thing per view: the next action or the thing to check.
Do reserve Decision Green-Teal for approvals, denials, acceptance and authorization, and nothing else.
Do separate beats with a 1px Hairline Stone top rule and 96px / 64px vertical padding.
Do caption every capture as real or as an illustration, and keep the caption under the image.
Do keep the exploded view's cartridges in the category fills, with the part number on the front face.
Do keep dashed lines for sockets, the agent layer, the branch and mating lines; they are the drawing's notation.
Do keep the connector notch on cartridges; it is the drawing's signature device.
Do keep every animation tied to a relationship or state change, and collapse it under reduced motion.
donts: Don't use purple or blue AI gradients, glowing brains, neural node clouds or particle fields.
Don't build fake browser, terminal or IDE chrome around screens. Real captures only, captioned as real.
Don't make icon-over-heading three-card feature grids, hero metric tiles or benchmark numbers.
Don't go dark-first or neon-on-black; light paper is primary.
Don't borrow Cognate-Workbench's cockpit styling (cobalt accent, Inter, Space Grotesk or JetBrains Mono) outside its captures.
Don't set type in Inter, Space Grotesk, Fraunces, IBM Plex Mono, Instrument Sans or Instrument Serif.
Don't add decorative motion. Every animation reveals a relationship or a state change.
Don't use Decision Green-Teal as a decorative accent or a heading color.
Don't add kicker or eyebrow labels above headings. The current ones are a defect the build carries, not a pattern to copy.
Don't use glyph icons or emoji as UI signifiers. The speed marker in the build is a defect, not a pattern.
Don't add drop shadows to cards or buttons. The sheet lift is the single exception.
Don't claim 'effortless', 'magic' or 'autonomous' as a selling point, or 'done' without evidence.
